entities.name: Antonio Maria Valsalva
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antonio Maria Valsalva was an Italian anatomist born in Imola. His research focused on the anatomy of the ears. He coined the term Eustachian tube and he described the aortic sinuses of Valsalva in his writings, published posthumously in 1740. His name is associated with the Valsalva antrum of the ear and the Valsalva maneuver, which is used as a test of circulatory function.

Anatomical structures bearing his name are Valsalva’s muscle and taeniae Valsalvae. He observed that when weakness of one side of the body is caused by a lesion in the brain, the culprit lesion tends to be on the side opposite (contralateral) to the weak side; this finding is named the "Valsalva doctrine" in his honor. Antonio Maria Valsalva was a physicians & medical pioneers from Imola (1666-06-17, Imola–1723-02-02). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Valsalva's discovery of the Eustachian tube and his description of the aortic sinuses of Valsalva had significant implications for the understanding of ear anatomy and its relationship to circulatory function. His work laid the foundation for later medical research and innovations.
